We are looking to build a machine learning model to predict the outcomes of (American) college football games in terms of final score and likelihood that a team covers the spread from Vegas This model ideally would use machine learning so it would become more accurate over time as it inputs new information. There are multiple components to consider: 1) Extracting relevant data from source(s) using an ongoing API integration 2) Data storage and hosting 3) Machine learning modeling

text:
I’m a passionate, hard-working machine learning freelancer with 6 years of experience building practical predictive systems. I’d be glad to help with your self-adjusting college football model across data ingestion, storage, and modeling.

In a telecom churn prediction project, I built a monthly churn score for 380k subscribers with per-customer SHAP reasons the retention team could read, reaching AUC 0.84 on a held-out quarter and 3.1x top-decile lift. In another project, I built a support ticket triage model that routed incoming tickets to 14 queues, and it improved macro-F1 to 0.88 from 0.62 while reducing median routing time from 6 hours to 4 minutes.

I have extensive experience with Python, scikit-learn, XGBoost, pandas, machine learning, and NLP-related workflows, and I’d be excited to discuss a system that improves as new game data comes in.
